name: Uptime Kuma
what_it_is: A self-hosted monitoring tool providing uptime tracking and alerting across HTTP(s), TCP, Ping, DNS, WebSocket, Docker containers, and more. It is a self-hosted alternative to services like Uptime Robot, with a reactive UI and 90+ notification integrations.
configuration: Custom status pages with custom domain mapping
modes: Active polling (HTTP, TCP, Ping, DNS, WebSocket, Steam)
Passive push (agent sends heartbeat to Uptime Kuma endpoint)
constraints: NFS (Network File System) is explicitly not supported as a data volume
Unsupported platforms: FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, Replit, Heroku
No built-in fault injection or synthetic failure simulation
No native SLA calculation or alert history reporting

docker_services.name: uptime-kuma
docker_services.notes: Official single-service compose; docker-compose.yml lives at repository root, not under docker/ subdirectory

notable_absences: No fault injection or chaos engineering support
No SLA / uptime percentage reporting built in
No built-in alert history or incident timeline
docker/docker-compose.yml path returned 404; compose file is at repository root
